gloss: World Cup — an international sports championship; in unqualified everyday Japanese usage, most often refers to the FIFA Football World Cup

definitions.gloss: World Cup — a global sports championship between national teams, especially the FIFA Football (Soccer) World Cup unless otherwise specified
definitions.explanation: Loanword from English "World Cup," used in Japanese for various international sports championships organized by a sport's world governing body. In the absence of a qualifier, ワールドカップ overwhelmingly refers to the FIFA Football World Cup ({サッカー}ワールドカップ), which receives massive media coverage in Japan and corresponds to most casual mentions of "the World Cup." Other sports use the same term as a compound — e.g., ラグビーワールドカップ (Rugby World Cup), {野球|やきゅう}ワールドカップ (Baseball World Cup; the equivalent for baseball is more typically called WBC, ワールド・ベースボール・クラシック). The abbreviation W{杯|はい} is widely used in newspaper headlines.

examples.japanese: ワールドカップを{見|み}る。
{日本|にほん}{代表|だいひょう}がワールドカップに{出場|しゅつじょう}した。
examples.english: The Japanese national team participated in the World Cup.

examples.japanese: {四年|よねん}に{一度|いちど}のワールドカップを{楽|たの}しみにしている。
examples.english: I'm looking forward to the World Cup, which is held once every four years.

examples.japanese: {二〇〇二年|にせんにねん}のワールドカップは、{日本|にほん}と{韓国|かんこく}の{共同|きょうどう}{開催|かいさい}だった。
examples.english: The 2002 World Cup was co-hosted by Japan and South Korea.

notes:
ワールドカップ is the loanword for "World Cup," the international championship held in many sports. In Japanese, unqualified ワールドカップ almost always refers to the FIFA Football World Cup; other sports clarify with a prefix.

DEFAULT MEANING IN CONTEXT:
- Without a sport qualifier → FIFA Football (Soccer) World Cup
- Held every four years; Japan has appeared at every tournament since 1998
- The 2002 edition was co-hosted by Japan and South Korea — the first World Cup held in Asia

COMMON COMPOUNDS / SPORT-SPECIFIC USAGE:
- {サッカー}ワールドカップ: FIFA Football World Cup (the explicit form)
- ラグビーワールドカップ: Rugby World Cup (Japan hosted in 2019)
- スキーワールドカップ: FIS Ski World Cup
- スノーボードワールドカップ: FIS Snowboard World Cup
- バレーボールワールドカップ: Volleyball World Cup
- フィギュアスケート (most often referred to as ISU{杯|はい} / GPシリーズ instead — not normally called ワールドカップ)
- Note: baseball's international championship is typically called the WBC (ワールド・ベースボール・クラシック), not ワールドカップ; cricket's is also called the Cricket World Cup but has limited Japanese coverage

ABBREVIATIONS IN MEDIA:
- W{杯|はい}: standard abbreviation in newspapers and headlines (W = World, {杯|はい} = cup)
- WC: occasional shorthand in writing
- ワールドカップ{予選|よせん}: World Cup qualifiers (often abbreviated to {W杯|だぶるはい}{予選|よせん} or simply {予選|よせん} in context)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ワールドカップに{出場|しゅつじょう}する: to participate in the World Cup
- ワールドカップで{優勝|ゆうしょう}する: to win the World Cup
- ワールドカップに{出|で}る: to play in the World Cup (more casual)
- ワールドカップを{開催|かいさい}する: to host the World Cup
- ワールドカップ{予選|よせん}: World Cup qualifiers
- ワールドカップ{本大会|ほんたいかい}: the World Cup finals (the tournament proper, as opposed to qualifiers)
- ワールドカップ{出場|しゅつじょう}{権|けん}: a berth at the World Cup
- ワールドカップを{制|せい}する: to claim the World Cup (literary / headline)

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- オリンピック: Olympics — the other major quadrennial international event
- {国際大会|こくさいたいかい}: international tournament (general term)
- {代表|だいひょう}: representative (team) — the national team that plays at the World Cup
- {予選|よせん}: qualifying round
- {決勝|けっしょう}: the final
- {優勝|ゆうしょう}: championship victory
- WBC (ワールド・ベースボール・クラシック): Baseball's equivalent international tournament

USAGE NOTES:
- Pronounced with two long vowels: わーるど (4 morae) + かっぷ (3 morae with the small っ as one mora)
- In casual speech, can be clipped: W{杯|はい} is read だぶるはい
- For specific tournaments, the year is appended: 2022 ワールドカップ, ワールドカップ・カタール{大会|たいかい}
- The English plural "World Cups" is rarely needed; if expressing multiple editions, Japanese uses {歴代|れきだい}のワールドカップ or {過去|かこ}のワールドカップ
